summary.headline: Ceigall Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 30.5% YoY to INR1,294 crores; FY27 guidance is minimum 15% revenue growth and 11-12.5% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest execution quarter of the year, with standalone revenue of INR1,294 crores (up 30.5% YoY) and standalone EBITDA of INR183 crores (14.1% margin). Full-year standalone revenue grew 14.3% to INR3,869 crores, while FY26 order inflow of INR11,332 crores far exceeded the INR5,000 crore guidance, taking the order book to INR18,554 crores. Management guided FY27 to at least 15% revenue growth, 11-12.5% EBITDA margin and at least INR5,500 crores of order inflow. Working-capital stretch (trade payables and unbilled revenue days both up sharply) and a large pending equity commitment for HAM and renewable projects were the main analyst focus, alongside the INR13,000 crore Romania bid.

segments.name: Road EPC and HAM (NHAI, MPRDC)
segments.commentary: Order book comprises 19 EPC projects, 10 HAM projects and 1 DBFOT project; all HAM projects are NHAI except one MPRDC project. Sahebganj-Areraj-Bettiah corridor (INR2,160 crores project cost) is the largest award to date.

segments.name: Renewable and power transmission
segments.commentary: Renewables are 19% of the order book across 7 projects; FY26 inflow was about 35.02% renewable. Solar and BESS awards include Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh solar projects, Morena BESS and the Velgaon 400 KV substation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at a minimum of 15%, described as conservative versus past 10-15% guidance.
Renewable sector to contribute about 20-25% of FY27 total revenue.
EBITDA margin guided at 11-12.5%, which management says applies to pure operations excluding other income.
FY27 order inflow guided at a minimum of INR5,500 crores.
Management expects roughly INR400 crores of HAM monetisation cash from NEO Asset Management: Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali in Q1, Bathinda-Dabwali in Q2, Jalbehra-Shahbad in Q3.
Equity requirement of about INR1,937 crores over three years, of which about INR800 crores is renewable and the rest HAM roads; more than INR400 crores already invested post-IPO.
capex_capacity: 37 ongoing projects in various stages of completion; Delhi-Amritsar-Katra Expressway achieved COD during FY26.

Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali HAM asset sold under a binding agreement with NEO Asset Management, described as the first such monetisation; Bathinda-Dabwali and Jalbehra-Shahbad are under non-binding offer and due diligence.

Solar Maharashtra: lease for more than 50 MW done, more than 75 MW expected this month; land development, fencing and piling started. Madhya Pradesh land leasing expected to close within about 10 days.
Morena BESS project awarded but not started: PPA not yet signed and transmission line tender not yet received; work depends on government land, transmission connectivity and PPA.
Velgaon 400 KV substation in Maharashtra in progress; transmission orders placed and T&D construction underway.
demand_pricing: Order inflow FY26 INR11,332 crores vs INR5,000 crores guidance; Q4 FY26 inflow INR6,014 crores across renewable and road. Book-to-bill about 4.8x.
Bids under evaluation about INR13,000 crores, including a 17 km Romania highway (highway, tunnel and bridges) where management says it was the only qualifying single bidder out of 12.
Sobha project in Dubai (about AED250 million) was also bid.
NHAI pipeline about INR2 lakh crores per management; company is bidding projects above INR2,000 crores and has a INR21,160 crore project and a INR600 crore Zirakpur bypass project.
Escalation clause changed from quarterly to monthly by MoRTH; billing plan eased to monthly payments after the recent war-related notifications.

qa_highlights.question: Pipeline for domestic and international business, and targets over one to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Offices opened in Singapore and Dubai, and a CEO International appointed. International expansion was slowed by the war; the company will bid abroad only if EBITDA margins and concessional IRRs are adequate.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue guidance of 15% looks low given the order book; what is the internal target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is being conservative; it had previously guided 10-15% and achieved it, and 15% minimum is intended as an easy-to-achieve floor.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and working capital plan?
qa_highlights.answer: MoRTH notifications moved billing from milestones to monthly payments; more than INR400 crores from NEO asset sales is expected, so management says cash flow is not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade payable days jump from 79 to 138 and unbilled revenue days from 94 to 133?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed it to March billing being paid by the department only in April, with creditor payments linked to receivables; about INR300 crores was paid to creditors in April. Unbilled revenue rose because milestone billing on large projects (10% per milestone, over INR100 crores each) lagged, and should improve with monthly billing.

qa_highlights.question: Margin drivers in Q4 and risk from iron ore and raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 margin was helped by four HAM projects started last year and higher turnover. Management said escalation is now paid monthly, so cost increases are passed through to the EPC contractor.

qa_highlights.question: Margins falling over three years as per the presentation slide 41?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said pure-operations EBITDA has stayed at 11-12.5% for three years; the earlier-year figures included bonus and royalty income (INR20 crores in FY25 and a Karnal-Pehowa bonus in FY24), which are included in revenue from operations.

qa_highlights.question: Equity investment needs and funding sources?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,937 crores is needed over three years (about INR800 crores renewable, rest HAM roads). Management cited unencumbered cash of about INR166 crores and FDR of about INR75 crores at March 31 (corrected from figures stated on the call), plus cash accruals and NEO proceeds.

risks_watch: Receivable and unbilled-revenue days rose sharply (unbilled 94 to 133 days; trade payables 79 to 138 days); watch whether monthly billing reverses this in coming quarters.

Large Romania bid (about INR13,000 crores) would be a major international entry and could be about 65-70% of the current order book; bid timing is uncertain and management said bid validity is nearing expiry.
Renewable projects depend on government land, PPAs and transmission connectivity; Morena BESS has not started.
HAM monetisation timing: only the Malout-Abohar-Sadhuwali deal is binding, and the other two sales remain at non-binding offer stage.
Margin guidance of 11-12.5% is excluding other income, which management said is volatile; FY26 standalone PAT margin was 7.9%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order inflow and growth, but guidance is repeatedly described as conservative. Evasive on segment-level margins and the Romania bid's economics; the call also had a corrected cash figure and a line disturbance.

So plain vanilla EPC would be minimum between 11% to 12.5%.
